title: 1957 AHSME Problem 1
statement: The number of distinct lines representing the altitudes, medians, and interior angle bisectors of a triangle that is isosceles, but not equilateral, is:

solutions.text:
The altitude, median, and angle bisector from the apex are the same line. At each of the two base vertices, those three lines are distinct. Thus there are \[ 1+3+3=7 \] distinct lines.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Separate the line from the apex from the lines drawn from the two base vertices
At the apex, the altitude, median, and angle bisector coincide; at either base vertex they do not
